after: ## The concept of a data structure
alt: Left: storing 30 marks without a data structure needs variables mark1 to mark30 and 30 separate additions. Right: an array called marks holds them all under one name with numbered indexes, and a single loop can total them whatever the number of marks.
caption: A data structure stores related items under one name so one loop can process them all.

alt: The array temps holds 14, 17, 21, 19 and 16 at indexes 0 to 4. temps[0] is 14 and temps[3] is 19; temps[1] ← 18 replaces 17; LEN(temps) is 5, so the last index is 4 and temps[5] does not exist.
caption: Indexes start at 0, so the last index is always one less than the length.

alt: Pseudocode that sets highest to temps[0] and loops from index 1 to LEN(temps) - 1. With temps holding 14, 18, 21, 19 and 16, highest starts at 14, becomes 18 at i = 1 and 21 at i = 2, and stays 21 for i = 3 and i = 4, so 21 is output.
caption: Start from the first element, then compare the rest one index at a time.

alt: The sales array as a grid of 3 shops (rows 0 to 2) by 4 days (columns 0 to 3). The first index selects the row and the second the column, so sales[1][2] is 4 (shop 1, day 2) and sales[2][0] is 9 (shop 2, day 0).
caption: Two indexes: the first picks the row, the second picks the column.

after: ## Worked example: totals from a two-dimensional array
alt: The sales grid with row totals 21, 15 and 23 for shops 0 to 2 and column totals 21, 18, 6 and 14 for days 0 to 3; both add up to a grand total of 59. Below, nested FOR loops reset shopTotal to 0 inside the outer loop and add sales[shop][day] along each row.
caption: Outer loop picks the row, inner loop walks along it; both directions give the same grand total, 59.

alt: A Pupil record p with four fields: name (String, "Farah"), yearGroup (Integer, 10), average (Real, 68.5) and hasLocker (Boolean, True). p.name gives Farah and p.average ← 70.0 changes one field; fields are reached by name, so p[1] is wrong. Equivalents: struct in C#, structure in Visual Basic, a class used without OOP in Python.
caption: A record’s fields can have different data types and are reached by name, not by index.

alt: The array form shown as a row of Pupil records, form[0], form[1], form[2] and so on, each with the fields name, yearGroup, average and hasLocker. The expression form[i].hasLocker is read left to right: form[i] selects a record, then .hasLocker selects a field inside it. A loop outputs the name of each pupil without a locker.
caption: Read left to right: the index picks the record, the dot picks the field.

alt: A decision tree. One item with several fields of mixed types: a record, such as one customer’s details. Many items each with mixed fields: an array of records, such as every customer. Many items of one type: a 1D array for a list, such as 12 monthly rainfall totals, or a 2D array for a grid, such as a chessboard or marks for 25 pupils in 6 tests.
caption: Same type in a list or grid: an array. Mixed types: a record. Many mixed items: an array of records.
